# coolify_s3_storage (Resource)

An S3-compatible storage used as a backup destination for databases.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "coolify_s3_storage" "backups" {
  name       = "db-backups"
  endpoint   = "https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"
  bucket     = "my-coolify-backups"
  region     = "eu-west-1"
  access_key = var.s3_access_key
  secret_key = var.s3_secret_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `access_key` (String, Sensitive) Access key id.
- `bucket` (String) Bucket name.
- `endpoint` (String) S3 endpoint URL, e.g. `https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` or a MinIO/Garage endpoint.
- `region` (String) Bucket region (any non-empty value for S3-compatible stores).
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) Secret access key.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form description. Coolify only accepts letters (including Unicode), numbers, whitespace, and `- _ . , ! ? ( ) ' " + = * @ / &` — other punctuation (e.g. a colon or semicolon) is rejected with a 422.
- `name` (String) Display name.

### Read-Only

- `is_usable` (Boolean) Whether Coolify validated connectivity to the bucket (via `ListObjectsV2`). `POST`/`PATCH /s3-storages` never set this themselves — Create/Update follow up with `POST /s3-storages/{uuid}/validate` so this reflects the real state instead of Coolify's own default of `false`, which otherwise sticks forever (nothing else calls that endpoint until a backup job happens to run). A `false` here after a successful apply means the connection check itself failed — see the warning diagnostic for why; `coolify_volume_backup` and `coolify_database_backup` both reject a storage in this state with a 422.
- `uuid` (String) Server-assigned identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import coolify_s3_storage.example <uuid>
```
